column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats a verb of descending for arrows and hand; BSB says pierced deeply and pressed down.
The Hebrew names flesh and peace; BSB says body and rest.
The Hebrew explicitly pictures iniquities passing over my head; BSB says overwhelmed me.
The Hebrew names folly without explicitly adding sinful as BSB does.
The Hebrew uses completed verbs of bending and going about; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew names burning without an explicit pain added by BSB.
The Hebrew says I roared, using a completed verb; BSB says I groan.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the light and they are not with me; BSB describes the light having faded.
The Hebrew describes standing opposite my affliction; BSB says shun my disease.
The Hebrew explicitly names my soul; BSB says my life.
The Hebrew has his mouth in a third-person description of a mute; BSB says I do not open my mouth.
The Hebrew has reproofs in the plural; BSB says no reply.
The Hebrew describes waiting as completed; BSB says I wait.
The Hebrew describes their exalting themselves over me with a completed verb; BSB says taunt me.
The Hebrew names limping and being before me; BSB says fall and with me.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names living enemies who have become strong; BSB describes many enemies without cause.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the Lord my salvation; BSB says my Savior.
